info.title: Qoblex Api v1 Documentation
info.description:
# Introduction

Welcome to the Qoblex API. Qoblex is the inventory, order, and production backbone behind the platform at https://go.qoblex.com, and this API gives your own systems the same operations your team relies on every day: managing products and stock, raising sale and purchase orders, fulfilling shipments, and reconciling invoices and payments.

The API is organized around [REST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer). It has predictable, resource-oriented URLs, accepts JSON-encoded request bodies, returns JSON-encoded responses, and uses standard HTTP verbs, response codes, and authentication. Every request is scoped to your own account, so you only ever read and change your own data.

All endpoints live under the `/v1` path. The API evolves additively: we may introduce new endpoints and response fields at any time, so build your integration to ignore fields it does not recognize. We will publish a new version in the path (for example `/v2`) before making a breaking change.

# Migrating from the legacy API

If you built against our previous API at `api.stockandbuy.com`, welcome to the new Qoblex API. This version is a significant step up: far richer resources, consistent REST conventions, expandable responses, filtering and sorting, and clearer errors. We worked hard to keep the transition smooth and preserved backward compatibility wherever we could, so most of what you already integrate carries across with little or no change.

A few things did change:

- **Authentication moved from Basic auth to an API key.** The legacy API authenticated with a username and password over HTTP Basic. The new API uses a single `qoblex-x-api-key` header instead (see [Authentication](#description/authentication)). Generate a key in your account and send it on every request.
- **A small number of breaking changes.** To deliver the richer data and cleaner contracts, we had to change a fraction of the endpoints and payloads. The great majority remain backward compatible; the exceptions are where the improved shape was clearly worth it.
- **New base path.** Requests now go to this API under its `/v1` path rather than `api.stockandbuy.com`.

> [!NOTE]
> Moving an existing integration over and not sure how a legacy call maps to the new API? [Contact us](mailto:support@qoblex.com?subject=Qoblex%20API%20migration) and we will help you map it across and flag anything that changed.

# Authentication

The Qoblex API authenticates every request with a single API key, sent in the `qoblex-x-api-key` header:

```http
qoblex-x-api-key: your_api_key
```

Your key carries the access of the integration it belongs to, so keep it secret: never share it in publicly accessible places such as GitHub, client-side code, or support tickets. All requests must be made over HTTPS; calls sent over plain HTTP, or without a valid key, fail with `401 Unauthorized`.

See [Managing API keys](#description/managing-api-keys) to create, revoke, and disconnect keys.

# Managing API keys

> [!NOTE]
> API access is a paid add-on. It is included and fully active during your free trial, so you can build and test straight away. After the trial, add it from [our pricing page](https://qoblex.com/pricing) to keep your integration live.

**Create an API key**

1. Sign in to your Qoblex account at https://go.qoblex.com.
2. Go to **Integrations** and find the **API** integration tile.
3. Click **Install**, then click **Create API key**.
4. Copy the key and send it as the `qoblex-x-api-key` header on every request.

**Revoke an API key**

1. Open the **API** integration under **Integrations**.
2. Find the key you want to revoke and click **Revoke API key**. Any request made with that key then fails with `401 Unauthorized`.

**Disconnect the integration**

To disable every API key at once and remove the integration, click **Disconnect** on the API integration screen. This revokes all keys and switches off API access until you install the integration again.

# Permissions and scopes

Access to the API is governed by permissions. Every API key inherits the permissions of the integration or team member it belongs to, so a key can only perform the actions that identity is allowed to perform.

Permissions are expressed as **scopes**, where a scope pairs a resource with an action:

- **Resources** are grouped by area of the product, for example `sales/orders`, `inventory/products`, `stock_control/purchase_orders`, `contacts/customers`, `reporting/sales`, `manufacturing`, `users`, and `integrations`.
- **Actions** describe what you may do with a resource: `view`, `create`, `edit`, `delete`, `authorize`, and `approve`.

A scope therefore reads naturally, such as "view sales orders" or "approve purchase orders". Grant each key only the scopes its integration actually needs.

> [!TIP]
> The permissions system is built and ready, and you can configure scopes today. We are switching enforcement on across the API area by area as we bring each part of the product onto our new experience, so anything you set now is future-proof: as each endpoint comes online it automatically respects the permissions you have already configured, with nothing for you to change.

# Errors

Qoblex uses conventional HTTP status codes to signal the outcome of a request. Codes in the `2xx` range mean success. Codes in the `4xx` range mean the request failed given the information provided, such as a missing field, an invalid key, or an unknown id. Codes in the `5xx` range mean something went wrong on Qoblex's side.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` OK | The request succeeded. |
| `204` No Content | The request succeeded and there is no body to return. |
| `400` Bad Request | The request was malformed or failed validation. |
| `401` Unauthorized | The API key is missing or invalid. |
| `402` Payment Required | API access is enabled but the account is not on a qualifying plan. |
| `403` Forbidden | The key is valid but not permitted to perform this operation. |
| `404` Not Found | The endpoint or resource does not exist. |
| `405` Method Not Allowed | The HTTP method is not supported on this endpoint. |
| `422` Unprocessable Entity | The request was well-formed but could not be processed. |
| `429` Too Many Requests | You have exceeded the rate limit. See [Rate limits](#rate-limits). |
| `500` Internal Server Error | Something went wrong on our end. |
| `503` Service Unavailable | The service was temporarily unable to handle the request. |

When a request fails validation, Qoblex returns `400` as an [RFC 7807](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7807) document whose `errors` object names each rejected field and why it was rejected:

```json
{
  "title": "One or more validation errors occurred.",
  "status": 400,
  "errors": {
    "email": ["The email field is required."]
  }
}
```

Rate-limited requests return `429` as an [RFC 7807](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7807) `application/problem+json` document:

```json
{
  "type": "https://httpstatuses.com/429",
  "title": "Too Many Requests",
  "status": 429,
  "detail": "API rate limit exceeded. Please retry after 42 seconds."
}
```

# Expanding responses

Many retrieve and list endpoints keep their default responses lean and let you pull in related data on demand with the `expand` query parameter. Pass a comma-separated list of expandable fields and Qoblex inlines them into the response, saving you a second request:

```text
GET /v1/sale_orders?expand=line_items.product_variant
```

Each endpoint documents the exact values it accepts. Expand values are case-insensitive, and requesting a value an endpoint does not support returns `400 Bad Request`.

# Filtering and sorting

List endpoints accept a `filters` and a `sort_by` query parameter so you can narrow and order results without pulling the whole collection. Each endpoint documents the fields it allows you to filter and sort on.

## Filtering

Pass `filters` as a comma-separated list of conditions. Each condition is a field, an operator, and a value, and conditions are combined with AND:

```text
GET /v1/products?filters=name@=shirt,quantity>10
```

Available operators:

| Operator | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `==` | Equals |
| `!=` | Not equals |
| `>` | Greater than |
| `<` | Less than |
| `>=` | Greater than or equal to |
| `<=` | Less than or equal to |
| `@=` | Contains |
| `_=` | Starts with |
| `_-=` | Ends with |
| `!@=` | Does not contain |
| `!_=` | Does not start with |
| `!_-=` | Does not end with |

Append `*` to any of the string operators for a case-insensitive match, for example `@=*`, `_=*`, `==*`, or `!=*`.

To match any of several values, separate them with a pipe: `filters=status==open|packed`. To apply one condition across several fields, group the fields in parentheses: `filters=(name|sku)@=shirt`. If a value itself contains a comma or a pipe, escape it with a backslash: `filters=name@=blue\,large`.

## Sorting

Pass `sort_by` as a comma-separated list of fields. Results are ordered by each field in turn; prefix a field with `-` for descending order:

```text
GET /v1/products?sort_by=-created_at,name
```

# Pagination

List endpoints return results in pages of up to 50 records. Paging is zero-based: request the first page with `page=0`, the next with `page=1`, and so on. List responses include the total count so you can tell when you have retrieved every record.

# Rate limits

Each API key may make up to **30 requests per 60 seconds**. The limit is applied per integration, so one API key can never use up another's capacity, and sessions in the Qoblex web app are unaffected.

Every response reports your current limit and how much of it remains:

```http
X-RateLimit-Limit: 30
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 29
```

When you exceed the limit, Qoblex returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header telling you how many seconds to wait before trying again:

```http
Retry-After: 42
```

Pace your calls using the headers above, and retry `429` responses with exponential backoff.

# Date formats

All date and time fields use [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) format, for example `2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00`. Date and time values passed as query parameters must always be URL encoded.

# Versioning

The Qoblex API is versioned in the URL path. This reference describes `v1`, and every request is made under `/v1`.

The following are backward-compatible changes that we may make at any time without releasing a new version, so your integration should tolerate them:

- Adding new endpoints, resources, or optional request parameters.
- Adding new fields to existing responses.
- Adding new values to existing enums, and new event types.
- Changing the order in which fields appear in a response.

When a change would break existing integrations, we release it under a new path version (for example `/v2`) and keep the current version running so you can migrate on your own schedule. Build defensively: read fields by name, ignore any you do not recognize, and do not depend on field ordering.

# Webhooks

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Webhooks are coming soon.** We are actively designing them and want to build the events you need first. [Tell us which webhooks would be most useful to you](mailto:support@qoblex.com?subject=Qoblex%20API%20webhooks) and we will factor your input into the rollout.

Webhooks will let Qoblex notify your systems in real time when events happen in your account, for example when an order is created, a shipment is dispatched, or stock changes, so you can react without polling. When they are released, this section will document the available event types, the payload format, and how to verify webhook signatures.

get.description:
Returns your account: the company profile that everything else in Qoblex hangs off. Read it to
see your account name, billing and warehouse locations, and base currency in one call, for
example when populating a settings screen or confirming which currency your reports are in.

200.description: Your account, including name, locations, and base currency.

get.description:
Returns the stores connected to your account: the sales channels and storefronts you sell
through, such as e-commerce platforms or B2B portals. Each store carries its name and host
URL, so you can tell your channels apart and match orders back to where they came from.

200.description: An array of connected stores, each with its id, name, and host URL.

get.description:
Returns the adjustment reasons your team can pick from when recording an inventory adjustment.
Use it to populate the reason dropdown so every adjustment is logged against a consistent,
account-defined reason.

200.description: An array of your adjustment reasons.

get.description:
Returns your account's locations: warehouses, stores, offices, and anywhere else you track
stock or ship from. Use it to populate location pickers on orders and transfers. Narrow the
list to only locations available on purchase orders, or only those allowed to hold inventory.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description:
Filters to apply on the location list: property operator value.
Supported properties:
- `id`
- `name`
- `type` (one of `Warehouse`, `Billing`, `Dropship`)
- `available_in_purchase_orders`
Supported operators:
`==` (equals), `!=` (not equals), `@=*` (contains, case-insensitive)
String values must be double-quoted. Combine multiple filters with `,` (AND) or `|` (OR), with a space on each side of the operator.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description:
Sorting to apply on the location list: prefix with - for descending, no prefix for ascending. Multiple sorts can be combined using commas.
Supported properties: `id`, `name`, `available_in_purchase_orders`.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Comma separated values of properties to expand on and include in the response. The following values are supported for expansion:
- `address`

200.description: An array of locations, each with its id, name, and purchase-order availability flag.

get.description: Retrieves the details of a single location by its identifier, such as its name, type, and address.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The location to retrieve. Example: `7`.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: Comma separated list of properties to expand. Example: `address`.

200.description: The location details.

404.description: The location was not found.

get.description:
Returns your activity feed so you can keep an eye on recent notifications and what has
changed across the business. Pass `source_id` to narrow the feed to a single order's
activity (such as a purchase order's approvals, receipts, and billing changes) instead of
the full company-wide feed.

200.description: A paginated list of activity feed entries.

post.description:
Creates a stock adjustment at a given location, so you can record a correction or a
stocktake result against your on-hand quantities. The location must be able to hold
inventory - Warehouse locations only can be adjusted. New adjustments always start in
`Draft` mode and leave inventory untouched until you authorize them via
`POST /v1/adjustments/{id}/authorize`, giving you room to review before anything posts.

200.description: Returns the newly created draft adjustment and its line items.

400.description: The request was invalid, or the location cannot hold inventory.

404.description: No location matched the given ID.

get.description:
Returns your stock adjustments, so you can browse the corrections and stocktakes recorded
across your locations. Results are sorted by creation date and returned in pages.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Adjustment page number to return.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: A filter expression used to narrow the results, for example `name@=shirt,quantity>10`. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview for the full list of operators and syntax.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: A sort expression: a comma-separated list of fields, each optionally prefixed with `-` for descending order. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview.

200.description: Returns a page of adjustments. Use the page parameter to walk through them all.

get.description:
Retrieves a single stock adjustment by its ID, so you can review a specific correction or
stocktake and its current state.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the stock adjustment. For example, `1024`.

200.description: Returns the full adjustment details.

404.description: No adjustment matched the given ID.

put.description:
Updates an existing draft stock adjustment, so you can revise a correction or stocktake
before it posts. You can change its line items, quantities, and adjustment details in a
single request.

200.description: Returns the updated adjustment and its line items.

400.description: The request was invalid, or the location cannot hold inventory.

401.description: You are not authorized to make this request.

404.description: No adjustment matched the given ID.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a draft stock adjustment, so you can discard a correction or stocktake
you no longer need. Only adjustments that have not been authorized can be deleted, since an
authorized adjustment has already changed your stock; to reverse one that has posted, create
a new adjustment instead.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the stock adjustment to delete. For example, `1024`.

200.description: Returns the ID of the deleted adjustment.

400.description: The adjustment has already been authorized and cannot be deleted.

401.description: You are not authorized to make this request.

404.description: No adjustment matched the given ID.

post.description:
Creates a new `Draft` adjustment by copying an existing one, handy for repeating a
recurring count at the same location. It copies the location, the reason, and the set of
product variants on the source's line items.
            
Every copied line starts as a no-op: `Set` to the variant's current on-hand quantity
at that location, exactly as if you had just added the variant by hand. Nothing moves in
your inventory until you enter your own counts, so the copy is safe to open and review.
            
Comments, the adjustment number, status, authorization date, scanning sessions, batch
assignments, reconciliation state, and quantity and cost variances are never carried over.
The copy is always a Simple adjustment attributed to you, and any line whose variant has
since been deleted, made untracked, or removed from your inventory is left out.
Adjustments in any status can be duplicated, including authorized ones, and the original
is never modified.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the adjustment to duplicate. For example, `1024`.

200.description: Returns the newly created draft adjustment and its line items.

400.description: The source adjustment has no location, or the location can no longer hold inventory.

404.description: No adjustment matched the given ID.

post.description:
Uploads a stocktake count CSV for a location and processes it in the background, one byte-range
chunk at a time, so very large variant catalogs no longer time out the request. Every field change
other than quantity/cost (buffer, min/max inventory, barcode, bin, overselling, supplier SKU) is
applied as its page is processed. Quantity and cost changes are collected across the whole file
into a single stock adjustment, created and authorized once as the last step. Poll the returned
job via `GET /v1/jobs` to follow progress and completion.

parameters.name: location_id
parameters.description: The location the stocktake count applies to.

200.description: The import job, in `Queued` status.

400.description: No file was uploaded, or the location cannot hold inventory.

404.description: No location matched the given ID.

post.description:
Reconciles a stocktake by writing the final approved quantity for one or more selected line items, turning raw scanner counts into the numbers you will post. Scanner counts are preserved as audit history and are not modified. Only line items explicitly included in the request are reconciled — others remain unchanged.

Every line to reconcile is listed in `items` by `line_item_id`. By default (`strategy: SetQuantity`) the caller also supplies `final_quantity` per line, as a single admin decision typed for one line at a time. To reconcile several selected lines at once without typing a quantity for each one, set `strategy` to `AcceptScanner`, `Merge`, `AcceptSystem`, or `AcceptSuggestion`; `final_quantity` is then ignored and the final quantity for each line is computed from the scanners' counts instead. A line that cannot be resolved with the chosen strategy (for example, the chosen scanner never counted it) is skipped rather than failing the request, and reported back in `skipped_lines`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the draft stocktake adjustment being reconciled.

requestBody.description: The reconcile strategy and the lines (and, for `SetQuantity`, final quantities) to reconcile.

200.description:
Returns the reconciled adjustment line items, each including the final quantity, variance,
cost impact, and the original scanner session lines as audit history, together with how many
requested lines were applied versus skipped.

400.description: The request is invalid or the stocktake cannot be reconciled.

404.description: The adjustment or required stocktake data was not found.

post.description:
Authorizes a draft adjustment, posting it to your inventory and locking the stocktake so it
becomes read-only. This is the step that actually moves your stock, so a stocktake can only be
authorized once every line has been reconciled. For batch-tracked lines you can pass batch
allocations in `line_items` and authorize in one request, instead of a separate call to
`POST /{id}/batches` first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the draft adjustment to authorize. For example, `1024`.

requestBody.description: Optional batch allocations for batch-tracked lines.

200.description: Returns the authorized, now read-only adjustment.

400.description: The stocktake has unreconciled lines, has under- or over-allocated batch-tracked lines, or cannot be authorized.

401.description: You are not authorized to make this request.

404.description: No adjustment matched the given ID.

get.description:
Returns the line items of a specific adjustment, so you can review the products, quantities, and variances that make it up. Results are paginated, and you can filter and sort them using the `filters` and `sort_by` query parameters.
Filterable/sortable properties: `id`, `product_variant.name`, `sku`, `reconciliation_status`, `operation`, `total`, `quantity`, `cost`, `quantity_variance`, `cost_variance`. Filterable only: `product_variant.is_batch_tracked`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the adjustment. For example, `1024`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to return.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: A filter expression used to narrow the results, for example `name@=shirt,quantity>10`. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview for the full list of operators and syntax.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: A sort expression: a comma-separated list of fields, each optionally prefixed with `-` for descending order. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of relations to expand in the response.
Supported values: - `session_lines`: include stocktake scan lines recorded per user for each item - `batch_usages`: include batch/lot allocations recorded for each batch-tracked item

200.description: Returns a page of the adjustment's line items.

401.description: You are not authorized to make this request.

404.description: No adjustment matched the given ID.

delete.description:
Removes selected line items from a draft adjustment, so you can drop products that were
added by mistake or should not be counted. Only the line items you name are deleted; the
rest of the adjustment is left untouched.

200.description:
Returns the IDs of the line items that were deleted. When a large batch is removed, only the
first 200 IDs are returned.

post.description:
Assigns batch-level quantities to the lines of a stock adjustment, so batch-tracked
stock is counted against the exact batches it belongs to. A single line item can be
split across several batches, and positive quantities add stock while negative
quantities remove it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the stock adjustment. For example, `1024`.

200.description: Confirms whether the batch assignments were saved: `true` on success, `false` otherwise.

post.description:
Creates and updates batches in a single request. Each item that carries an `id` updates that
batch (for example its lot number, expiry date, or on-hand quantity); each item without an
`id` creates a new batch for its variant. Setting a quantity on either records the change as
an auto-authorized inventory adjustment; a new batch starts at zero, so its full quantity is
adjusted in. The whole request is applied together: if any item fails, none of the changes are saved.

200.description:
The created and updated batch records, each with its location, variant, quantity, and expiry
information.

get.description:
Retrieves your batches. Filter and sort by any supported field to surface batches nearing expiry
or low on stock - for example narrow to a single variant with `filters=product_variant.id==4821` -
and page through large accounts.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: A filter expression used to narrow the results, for example `name@=shirt,quantity>10`. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview for the full list of operators and syntax.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: A sort expression: a comma-separated list of fields, each optionally prefixed with `-` for descending order. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview.

200.description:
A paginated list of batch records, each with location, variant, quantity, reserved quantity, cost,
and expiry information.

delete.description:
Deletes a batch, letting you clean up lots you no longer track. Deleting a batch that still holds
stock or has active reservations can cause inventory discrepancies, so delete only batches with a
quantity of zero.

parameters.name: batch_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the batch to delete. Example: `9032`.

200.description:
The deleted batch record, including its location, variant, quantity, and expiry information as
they stood at the time of deletion.

get.description:
Retrieves end-to-end traceability for a batch, showing where its stock originated (upstream)
and where it was consumed or shipped (downstream). Use it for quality control, product
recalls, and inventory audits across receipts, sales, transfers, adjustments, returns, and
manufacturing orders.

parameters.name: batch_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the batch to trace. Example: `9032`.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: The tracing direction.

200.description:
The batch trace, with a summary of all quantity movements and a detailed list of its upstream
and downstream operations.

post.description:
Records a payment made to the supplier against an authorized bill, reducing the amount still due.
Payments can only be added to bills that have been authorized.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: bill_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill.

200.description: The purchase order with the new payment recorded.

post.description: Updates a payment already recorded against a bill, for example to correct its amount or date.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: bill_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill.

parameters.name: payment_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the payment.

200.description: The purchase order with the updated payment.

delete.description:
Permanently removes a payment recorded against a bill, for example one entered in error, and restores
that amount to the bill's amount due.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: bill_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill.

parameters.name: payment_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the payment.

200.description: The purchase order without the removed payment.

post.description:
Creates a draft bill against a purchase order for the line items and landed costs you specify, so you
can record what the supplier is invoicing you. The bill starts as a draft; authorize it separately once
it's ready to be paid.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

200.description: The purchase order with the new draft bill included.

get.description:
Retrieves a single bill on a purchase order, with its calculated totals, amount paid, amount due,
and whether it can still take a payment. These figures are the source of truth for what the supplier
is owed, so show payment amounts from here rather than adding them up yourself.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: bill_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill.

200.description: The requested bill, with its totals, amount paid, and amount due.

404.description: No purchase order with this id, or no matching bill, exists in your account.

patch.description:
Use this API endpoint to amend a bill that hasn't been authorized yet: its number, dates,
supplier reference and notes, along with the quantity, price and discount of its lines.
Dropping a line is a separate operation - delete the line item or landed cost item directly.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: bill_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill.

requestBody.description: The amendments to apply. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

200.description: Returns the updated bill with recalculated totals.

400.description: Returned when the bill is already authorized or an amendment is invalid.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a draft bill that hasn't been authorized yet, for example one entered in error.
Only drafts can be deleted, authorize must be reverted first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: bill_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill.

200.description: The purchase order without the deleted bill.

post.description:
Authorizes a draft bill, recording the billed amount as owed to the supplier and making it available
for payment. This is the step that turns a draft into a payable liability.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: bill_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill.

200.description: The purchase order with the authorized bill.

post.description:
Reverts an authorized bill back to draft so you can correct it, undoing its recognition as an amount
owed to the supplier.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: bill_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill.

200.description: The purchase order with the bill reverted to draft.

delete.summary: Remove a line item from a draft bill
delete.description:
Use this API endpoint to drop a purchase order line item from a bill that hasn't been
authorized yet. A bill always keeps at least one line - delete the bill itself instead.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: bill_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill.

parameters.name: line_item_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill line item.

200.description: Returns the bill without the removed line, with recalculated totals.

400.description: Returned when the bill is authorized or this is its last remaining line.

delete.summary: Remove a landed cost item from a draft bill
delete.description:
Use this API endpoint to drop a landed cost item from a bill that hasn't been authorized yet.
A bill always keeps at least one line - delete the bill itself instead.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: bill_id

parameters.name: landed_cost_item_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill landed cost item.

post.description:
Turns a simple variant into a bundle or a bill of material made up of component variants, so you can build
kit and manufacturing structures in your catalog. A bundle is sold and shipped as its parts; a bill of
material is assembled into the variant through a manufacturing order. Bundles must use standard stock
tracking, while a bill of material may be batch or serial tracked. Components can themselves be bills of
material, so multi-level structures are supported. The supplied components are the complete set for the
variant. To amend the components of an already-composed variant, use the component endpoints; to change its
type, dismantle it first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the variant to compose. Example: `4821`.

200.description: The variant's new composition, including its type and component lines.

400.description: The request is invalid, for example an unknown type, an empty component set, a self-reference, or a plain bundle used as a component.

404.description: No variant with the given id exists in your account.

delete.description:
Dismantles a bundle or bill-of-material variant back into a simple variant, removing all of its components.
Use this to undo a composition or to change a variant's type before composing it again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the composed variant to dismantle. Example: `4821`.

200.description: The variant after dismantling, now simple with no component lines.

400.description: The variant is already simple and has no composition to dismantle.

404.description: No variant with the given id exists in your account.

post.description:
Adds a component to a composed variant, or updates its quantity when the `component_variant_id` is
already present (the component is matched, and upserted, by that id). Use this to amend a bundle or bill of
material without rebuilding it. The variant must already be a bundle or bill of material.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the composed variant. Example: `4821`.

200.description: The variant's composition after the component was added or updated.

400.description: The request is invalid, for example the variant is simple, a self-reference, or a plain bundle used as a component.

404.description: No variant with the given id exists in your account.

delete.description:
Removes a single component from a composed variant. Removing the last remaining component dismantles the
variant back into a simple variant.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the composed variant. Example: `4821`.

200.description: The variant's composition after the component was removed.

400.description: The request is invalid, for example the variant is simple or the component is not part of it.

404.description: No variant with the given id exists in your account.

get.description: Returns every currency code Qoblex supports, in ISO 4217 format (for example USD, EUR, GBP). Use these codes when setting the currency on orders, price lists, and other financial records.

200.description: An array of supported ISO 4217 currency code strings, such as USD, EUR, and GBP.

get.description: Retrieves the current market exchange rate between two currencies, for example to pre-fill the rate when creating an order in a foreign currency. Both `from` and `to` must be ISO 4217 codes.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The source ISO 4217 currency code, for example `USD`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The target ISO 4217 currency code, for example `EUR`.

200.description: The exchange rate as a decimal from the source currency to the target currency.

post.description:
Creates a custom field and attaches it to a single record, so you can store extra data
on an order, product, or contact beyond the built-in fields. Use this to capture the
details your business tracks that the standard record does not hold.

200.description:
The newly created custom field, with its configuration, ownership, stored value, and
audit timestamps.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of custom fields, so you can see the extra data your team has
attached to orders, products, contacts, and other records. Each field carries its
definition, stored value, data type, editability, and which record it belongs to.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: A filter expression used to narrow the results, for example `name@=shirt,quantity>10`. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview for the full list of operators and syntax.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: A sort expression: a comma-separated list of fields, each optionally prefixed with `-` for descending order. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview.

parameters.name: include_count
parameters.description: Indicates whether the total record count should be included in the response.

200.description:
A paginated list of custom fields with their definitions, values, ownership, data types,
and editability settings.

delete.description:
Deletes a custom field value from a single record, such as an order or product, when the
extra data no longer applies. This clears the value for that one record only; the custom
field definition and the values held by other records are untouched.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the custom field value to delete, for example `4821`.

200.description: A success confirmation once the custom field value has been deleted.

post.description:
Assigns existing custom field definitions to a single record such as an order, product,
or contact, so the record is ready to hold that extra data. Use this to attach the fields
your team has already defined to the records where you want to capture their values.

200.description:
The custom fields now assigned to the record, with their configuration, current values,
and metadata.

post.description:
Creates a custom field definition for a chosen record type, setting up an extra field
your team can then fill in on orders, products, or contacts. The definition sets the
label, data type, allowed options, grouping, and editability that every value will follow.
The key must be unique for that record type.

200.description:
The newly created custom field definition, with its configuration, metadata, ownership
type, and identifiers.

400.description: A custom field definition with the same key already exists for this record type.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of custom field definitions, so you can see the extra fields
your team has set up before attaching values to records. A definition sets the label,
data type, options, and editability that every value of that field will follow.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: A filter expression used to narrow the results, for example `name@=shirt,quantity>10`. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview for the full list of operators and syntax.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: A sort expression: a comma-separated list of fields, each optionally prefixed with `-` for descending order. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview.

parameters.name: include_count
parameters.description: Indicates whether the total record count should be included in the response.

200.description:
A paginated list of custom field definitions with their configuration, ownership, value
types, display settings, available options, and editability rules.

put.description:
Updates a custom field definition, so a change to its label, data type, allowed options,
grouping, or editability applies everywhere the field is used. The change flows down to
every order or product that already holds a value, keeping the field consistent across
your records.
            
The field's key cannot be changed. Renaming the display name relabels the field without
detaching it from the records that already store a value.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the custom field definition to update, for example `317`.

200.description:
The updated custom field definition, with its configuration, metadata, ownership type,
and identifiers.

409.description:
The requested options would remove a value that orders or products still store. The
message lists those values; keep the options or clear the records first.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a custom field definition, retiring an extra field your team no longer
needs so it can't be used on future records. Use this to tidy up unused fields; check its
usage first, since records that still store a value must be cleared beforehand.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the custom field definition to delete, for example `317`.

200.description: A success confirmation once the custom field definition has been deleted.

get.description:
Retrieves which products and orders still store a value for a custom field definition,
so you can see where the field is in use before you delete it. Use this to warn before
removing a definition and to jump straight to the records that must be cleared first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the custom field definition to inspect, for example `317`.

200.description:
The products and orders that still hold a value for the definition, plus an
`in_use` flag showing whether it can be safely deleted.

post.description:
Creates a new customer so you can start quoting, selling, and invoicing against
the account right away. Include the customer's contact details, addresses, employees,
and account information such as payment terms and tax identification numbers.

200.description: The full created customer record, including contact details, addresses, and associated employees.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of your customers so you can browse your customer base,
keep a CRM or other system in sync, and pull records into order and reporting workflows.
Each customer carries its identity and contact details, addresses, tax identifiers,
payment terms, and the employees linked to the account.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: A filter expression used to narrow the results, for example `name@=shirt,quantity>10`. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview for the full list of operators and syntax.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: A sort expression: a comma-separated list of fields, each optionally prefixed with `-` for descending order. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview.

200.description:
A paginated list of customers, each with contact details, addresses, employees,
and account information.

get.description:
Retrieves a single customer's complete profile so you can view or reconcile
everything on file for one account. The record includes contact details, addresses,
linked employees, and account settings such as payment terms and tax identification numbers.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the customer. For example, `4521`.

200.description: The full customer record, including contact details, addresses, and associated employees.

post.description:
Records a deposit paid to the supplier up front against a purchase order, common when a supplier
requires payment before shipping. You can later allocate the deposit towards a bill on the same order.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

requestBody.description: The deposit to record, stated either as an amount or as a percentage of the order total.

200.description: The purchase order with the new deposit.

400.description: Returned when neither an amount nor a percentage is supplied, when both are, or when the value is out of range.

404.description: Not Found

patch.description:
Corrects the amount, reference or payment date of a deposit, for example when the amount was keyed in
wrongly. Only the fields you supply are changed. A deposit can no longer be changed once
it has synced to your accounting system, because that push is one-way; nor while it is allocated to a
bill - remove the allocation first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: deposit_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the deposit.

requestBody.description: The changes to apply, stated either as an amount or as a percentage of the order total.

200.description: The purchase order with the updated deposit.

400.description: Returned when the deposit has already been synced to your accounting system or allocated to a bill, or the new value is invalid.

404.description: Returned when the purchase order or the deposit does not exist.

delete.description: Permanently removes a supplier deposit from a purchase order, for example one recorded in error.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: deposit_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the deposit.

200.description: The purchase order without the deleted deposit.

post.description:
Applies a supplier deposit towards a bill's amount due, so a prepayment offsets what you owe on that
bill rather than paying it again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: deposit_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the deposit.

parameters.name: bill_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill to allocate the deposit to.

200.description: The purchase order with the deposit allocated to the bill.

delete.description:
Removes a supplier deposit's allocation from a bill, freeing the deposit back up so it can be applied
elsewhere or the bill's amount due can be paid another way.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: deposit_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the deposit.

parameters.name: bill_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the bill the deposit is allocated to.

200.description: The purchase order with the allocation removed.

post.description:
Records a draft refund owed to you by the supplier for goods or charges on a purchase order, for
example money back on returned or overbilled items. The refund starts as a draft; authorize it separately
once it's ready.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

200.description: The purchase order with the new draft refund included.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a draft supplier refund that hasn't been authorized yet, for example one raised in
error. Only drafts can be deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: refund_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the refund.

200.description: The purchase order without the deleted refund.

post.description:
Authorizes a draft supplier refund, confirming the amount the supplier owes you back. Only draft
refunds can be authorized.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: refund_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the refund.

200.description: The purchase order with the authorized refund.

post.description:
Reverts an authorized supplier refund back to draft so you can correct it. The refund stays
authorized if its synced credit note already has allocations applied against it in your accounting
system, the credit note is only deleted or voided there if the refund is later actually deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: refund_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the supplier refund.

200.description: The supplier refund, now back in draft status.

404.description: No purchase order with this id, or no matching supplier refund, exists in your account.

post.description:
Records goods arriving against a purchase order by creating a draft goods receipt note. Omit
line_items to receive the full remaining quantity on every line, or send specific line items and
quantities for a partial delivery. The note starts as a draft, authorize it separately to move the
stock into inventory.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

requestBody.description: The receiving location, carrier, tracking details, and the line items and quantities to receive.

200.description: The newly created draft goods receipt note.

404.description: No purchase order with this id exists in your account.

get.description:
Retrieves a single goods receipt note by its identifier, with its line items and any batches
assigned to them, so you can review exactly what was received. Use the expand parameter to pull in
related detail in the same call.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: grn_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the goods receipt note.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of related resources to include in the response.
Supported values:
- `order_items` — include the purchase order line item each receipt line was created against.
- `batches` — include the batch number and expiry date for each batch usage.

200.description: The requested goods receipt note.

404.description: No purchase order with this id, or no matching goods receipt note, exists in your account.

patch.description:
Updates a draft goods receipt note, for example to correct the receiving location, carrier, tracking
details, comments, or received quantities before you authorize it. Only the fields you send are changed,
and updates are only allowed while the note is still a draft.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: grn_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the goods receipt note.

requestBody.description: The fields and received quantities to change. Omitted fields keep their current value.

200.description: The updated goods receipt note.

400.description: The goods receipt note is already authorized, or a quantity exceeds what's still receivable.

404.description: No purchase order with this id, or no matching goods receipt note, exists in your account.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a draft goods receipt note, for example one created in error before the goods
were actually received. Only drafts can be deleted, once a note is authorized its stock has already
moved into inventory and it can no longer be removed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: grn_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the goods receipt note.

200.description: The deleted goods receipt note.

400.description: The goods receipt note is already authorized and cannot be deleted.

404.description: No purchase order with this id, or no matching goods receipt note, exists in your account.

post.description:
Authorizes a draft goods receipt note, moving its line items into inventory so on-hand stock reflects
the delivery. Authorizing also spreads any landed costs across the received items, so this is the step
that finalizes both stock levels and the true cost of what you received.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: grn_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the goods receipt note.

200.description: The authorized goods receipt note.

404.description: No purchase order with this id, or no matching goods receipt note, exists in your account.

post.description:
Records which specific batches or lots you received for each product on a goods receipt note, so
batch-tracked stock stays accurate for traceability and recalls. You can split one line item across
several batches, and set expiry dates on batches where that applies.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: grn_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the goods receipt note.

200.description: The resulting batch inventory records, showing the updated stock quantity for each batch after the receipt.

delete.summary: Delete Goods Receipt Note Line Item
delete.description:
Removes a single line item from a draft goods receipt note, for example a product that didn't
actually arrive in this delivery. Only allowed while the note is still a draft, and only when it's
not the last remaining line, a receipt must always keep at least one item.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: grn_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the goods receipt note.

parameters.name: line_item_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the goods receipt note line item.

200.description: The updated goods receipt note.

400.description: The goods receipt note is already authorized, or the line item is the last remaining one.

404.description: No purchase order with this id, no matching goods receipt note, or no matching line item, exists in your account.

post.description:
Creates a draft invoice for a sale order, the first step in billing the customer. The invoice
starts as a draft so you can review it; authorize it with the invoice authorization endpoint
once it's ready to count toward payment and reporting.

200.description: The sale order with its new invoice details.

post.description:
Authorizes a draft invoice, moving it from `Draft` to `Authorized` so it becomes a
finalized invoice that counts toward payment and reporting. Run this after reviewing the draft
invoice created for the order.

200.description: The authorized invoice.

post.description:
Records a payment received against a sale order, keeping the order's paid and outstanding
balances current as your customer settles up. The amount is given in the presentment currency
(the currency shown to the customer), along with the exchange rate used to convert it to your
base currency.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to record the payment against.

200.description: The updated sale order with the payment applied.

post.description:
Creates a new manufacturing order in draft. Provide the finished product variant to build (it must
be a bill of materials), the quantity to produce, the manufacturing location, and the manufacturer.
The order's component line items are copied from the finished variant's bill of materials, scaled to
the quantity you are producing; you can then add, amend, or remove them per order via the update
endpoint without changing the product's bill of materials. Start the order when you are ready to
reserve stock and move it into production.

200.description: The created manufacturing order, in draft.

400.description: The order could not be created, for example the variant is not a bill of materials, the quantity is not positive, the order number is already in use, or a referenced location or manufacturer does not exist.

get.description:
Returns your manufacturing orders, most recent first, in pages. Use this to browse production
work across its lifecycle, filter by status or manufacturer, and page through the full set to
build your own production view.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Specifies the page number for pagination.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of related resources to include in the response.
Supported values:
- `line_items.product_variant` — include each line item's variant details (sku, name, image).

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description:
Filters to apply on the manufacturing order list: property operator value.
Supported properties:
- `id`
- `number`
- `reference`
- `type` — `ProductionAssembly` or `ProductionDisassembly`.
- `status` — `Draft`, `InProduction`, `Completed`, or `Canceled`.
- `stock_status` — `AwaitingStock`, `ReadyToShip`, or `Fulfilled`.
- `manufacturer_id`
- `manufacturer.name`
- `bill_of_material_variant_id` — the finished product variant being produced.
- `location` — the manufacturing location id.
- `created_at`
- `updated_at`
- `tag`
- `deleted` — soft-deleted orders are included by default; filter `deleted==false` to exclude them.
Supported operators:
`==` (equals), `!=` (not equals), `@=*` (contains, case-insensitive), `>=` (greater than or equal) `<=` (less than or equal)
String values must be double-quoted (e.g. `manufacturer.name@=*"acme"`). Combine multiple filters with `,` (AND) or `|` (OR), with a space on each side of the operator.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description:
Sorting to apply on the manufacturing order list: prefix with - for descending, no prefix for ascending. Multiple sorts can be combined using commas. Defaults to `-created_at` (newest first) when omitted.
Supported properties:
- `id`
- `number`
- `reference`
- `type`
- `status`
- `stock_status`
- `manufacturer.name`
- `location`
- `created_at`
- `updated_at`
- `tag`
- `deleted`
Sorting is not supported on `manufacturer_id` or `bill_of_material_variant_id`.

200.description: A page of manufacturing orders. Use the page parameter to walk through all of your orders.

get.description:
Retrieves a single manufacturing order by its identifier, with the finished product it builds,
its planned quantity, the manufacturer and location, and its component line items,
so you can show a full production view in one call.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the manufacturing order.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of related resources to include in the response.
Supported values:
- `line_items.product_variant` — include each line item's variant details (sku, name, image).

200.description: The requested manufacturing order.

404.description: No manufacturing order with this id exists in your account.

post.description:
Updates a draft manufacturing order, changing only the fields you send and leaving everything
else as it was. Send an empty string to clear a text field. The order's component line items
start as a copy of the product's bill of materials, but you can add, amend, or remove them per
order without changing the product's bill of materials: when you send `line_items` it
replaces the order's current components (keep or amend a line by including its `id`, add a
line by omitting the `id`, and remove a line by leaving it out). A manufacturing order can
only be edited while it is in draft.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the manufacturing order to update.

200.description: The updated manufacturing order.

400.description: The order could not be updated, for example it is not in draft, the order number is already in use, or a line item is invalid.

404.description: No manufacturing order with this id exists in your account.

post.description:
Starts production on a draft manufacturing order. This reserves the components the order needs
from stock and moves the order into production. The order must be in draft, and there must be
enough component stock, otherwise the request is rejected with the reason.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the manufacturing order to start.

200.description: The manufacturing order, now in production.

400.description: The order could not be started, for example it is not in draft or components are out of stock.

404.description: No manufacturing order with this id exists in your account.

post.description:
Stops an in-production manufacturing order and returns it to draft, releasing the components it
had reserved back to available stock so the order can be edited again. Use this to undo a start
before the order is completed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the manufacturing order to stop.

200.description: The manufacturing order, back in draft.

400.description: The order could not be stopped, for example it is already completed or canceled.

404.description: No manufacturing order with this id exists in your account.

post.description:
Completes an in-production manufacturing order. This consumes the reserved components and adds
the finished goods to stock at the manufacturing location, closing out the production run. The
order must be in production. For batch-tracked production you can pass the finished and consumed
batches in the request body: they are recorded and the order is completed in a single step, so
batch traceability and completion succeed or fail together. The body is optional; omit it to
complete an order whose batches were already assigned. Supply the finished batches either as an
explicit `finished_batches` list or through the `batch_generator`, but not both.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the manufacturing order to complete.

requestBody.description: Optional finished and consumed batch assignments to record before completing.

200.description: The completed manufacturing order.

400.description: The order could not be completed, for example it is still a draft, its batch assignments are incomplete, both a finished-batch list and a generator were supplied, a finished or consumed batch quantity is not greater than zero, finished batch numbers repeat, the generator expression is invalid, or a consumed batch does not reference a batch_id.

404.description: No manufacturing order with this id exists in your account.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of your price lists. Price lists let you offer custom or tiered
pricing to different customers, so a regular customer and a preferred one can each see the
prices you set for them. Use this to review the price lists you have defined and how they
apply across your customer base.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Products page number to return

200.description: A paginated list of your price lists.

post.description:
Updates prices for one or more variants across your price lists in a single request, so you
can roll out pricing changes efficiently across customers, channels, or pricing tiers.

200.description:
A boolean indicating whether the price update was applied to every variant price entry you
provided.

post.description:
Creates a product together with any variants included in the request, as one consistent
catalog record. The options and variant option values must describe the same matrix, and
duplicate option combinations are rejected.
            
Variant stock quantities are not accepted here: warehouse operations own stock levels,
allocations, incoming quantities, and location balances.

200.description: The newly created product, returned in the same shape as Get Product.

400.description: Bad Request

get.description:
Returns your products, so you can browse or sync your full catalog into another system.
Products are sorted by their identifier and returned in pages of up to 50, so you page
through the list rather than pulling everything at once.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Products page number to return

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Comma separated values of properties to expand on and include in the response. The following values are supported for expansion:
- `variants`
- `images`
- `mappings`
- `variant.locations`
- `variant.price_lists`
- `variant.components`

schema.example: 'images,variant.components' => - expands the response to include variant components and image

parameters.example: 'images,variant.components' => - expands the response to include variant components and image

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: A filter expression used to narrow the results, for example `name@=shirt,quantity>10`. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview for the full list of operators and syntax.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: A sort expression: a comma-separated list of fields, each optionally prefixed with `-` for descending order. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview.

200.description:
The page of products, sorted by identifier. Use the `page` parameter to walk through
every product; each page contains at most 50 products.

get.description:
Retrieves the full details of a single product by its identifier, so you can look up its
variants, SKUs, and catalog data for one item without paging through the whole list.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the product to retrieve, for example `1024`.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Comma separated values of properties to expand on and include in the response. The following values are supported for expansion:
- `variants`
- `images`
- `mappings`
- `variant.locations`

can be received and closed for what did arrive. The new back order copies the supplier, ship-to and
billing locations, price list, currency, exchange rate, tax-inclusive setting, and due date, and contains
only the moved quantities. The two orders are linked, with the back order shown as a related order of the
original. Comments, tags, notes, and custom lines (landed costs) are not carried over.

order. Otherwise only the line items you list move, at the quantities you give.

line and leaves the received quantity behind. Once every remaining line is fully received, the original
order becomes Received. A line that has already been billed, or that a draft goods receipt note still
refers to, cannot be moved. Either the whole move succeeds or nothing changes.
            
An order where nothing has been received cannot have all of its line items moved out, since that would
leave it empty - delete or close it instead.
            
Note that a draft goods receipt note on a line that was only reduced may now ask for more than the line
has left, which is reported when that goods receipt note is authorized.

trend undamped and 0 removes it entirely. Ignored by the other forecast methods.

parameters.name: variant_scope

The forecasting report: detailed forecast lines plus optional summary totals, based on the time
range, stock coverage, and supplier strategy you configured.

summary.description: Aggregated totals for the report, when available.

get.description:
Returns the filters you can apply across the sales, purchase, inventory, and forecasting reports.
Use this to populate filter pickers when building a report, so you know which dimensions are
available before you run a query.

200.description:
The list of available reporting filters, covering dimensions such as product categories, warehouses,

post.description:
Creates a new sale order, a customer's request to purchase one or more products from your shop.
A sale order created through the API starts as a Quote and no inventory is reserved yet, so you
can build up and adjust the order before committing stock to it. To reserve inventory once the
order is ready, use the Allocate endpoint.

200.description: The newly created sale order.

get.description:
Returns a paginated list of your sale orders together with their related detail:
line items, payments, shipments, invoices, refunds, returns, and current order status.
This is the endpoint operators use to browse and reconcile orders across the fulfillment
and billing lifecycle in one call.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number used for pagination.

parameters.name: created_at_min
parameters.description: Enter a specific creation date for a sales order to return records created after that date. (ISO 8601 format)

parameters.name: created_at_max
parameters.description: Enter a specific creation date for a sales order to return records created before that date. (ISO 8601 format)

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Comma separated values of properties to expand on and include in the response.
Commonly used values: `customer`, `customer.addresses`, `invoices`, `shipments`, `refunds`, `returns`, `addresses`, `custom_fields`, and `line_items.product_variant` to include each line item's variant details (sku, name, cost, image). Also supports `sale_agent`, `price_list`, `allocations`, `deposits`, `related_orders`, `invoices.invoice_items`, and `invoices.custom_items`, matching the single sale order GET endpoint.

parameters.name: status[]
parameters.description: Sales order status to apply

items.description:
Ideally, we should use the states under Global but those contain more states than we need.
This represents the states we need to expose via the sales APIs.

parameters.name: updated_at_min
parameters.description: Enter a specific update date for a sales order to return records updated after that date

parameters.name: updated_at_max
parameters.description: Enter a specific update date for a sales order to return records updated before that date.

parameters.name: shipping_status[]
parameters.description: Sale order shipping status to apply

parameters.name: stock_status[]
parameters.description: Sale order stock status to apply

parameters.name: invoice_status[]
parameters.description: Sale order invoice status to apply

parameters.name: payment_status[]
parameters.description: Sale order payment status to apply

parameters.name: assignee_ids[]
parameters.description: Filters sales orders based on the provided assignee IDs.

parameters.name: location_ids[]
parameters.description: Filters sales orders based on the provided location IDs.

parameters.name: variant_ids[]
parameters.description: Filters sales orders based on the provided variant IDs.

parameters.name: tags[]
parameters.description: Filters sales orders based on the provided tags.

parameters.name: include_deleted

parameters.name: reference
