parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Searches by order number

200.description:
A paginated list of sale orders, each with its related invoices, shipments, refunds,
returns, allocations, and payments.

get.description:
Retrieves a single sale order by its ID, with the full detail you need to inspect one
order: its line items, payments, shipments, invoices, refunds, returns, and status.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to retrieve.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of related resources to include in the response.
Supported values:
- `invoices`
- `invoices.invoice_items`
- `invoices.custom_items`
- `shipments`
- `refunds`
- `returns`
- `returns.return_items`
- `returns.return_custom_items`
- `returns.exchange_line_items`
- `addresses`
- `customer`
- `customer.addresses`
- `sale_agent`
- `integration`
- `price_list`
- `allocations`
- `deposits`
- `custom_fields`
- `related_orders`

200.description: The sale order matching the given ID.

post.description:
Updates an existing sale order, changing only the fields you supply in the request body and
leaving everything else untouched. Some fields lock once the order progresses: currency,
exchange rate, tax-inclusive, and price list can no longer be changed once the order has been
invoiced, and customer, origin location, currency, exchange rate, tax-inclusive, price list,
and delivery date can no longer be changed once the order is closed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to update.

200.description: The updated sale order.

post.description:
Opens a sale order, moving it from Draft to Open so it becomes an active order ready for
fulfillment and billing. This is the step that promotes a draft into your live order flow.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to open.

200.description: The updated sale order with its status set to Open.

post.description:
Marks a sale order as Closed, its completed end state, once the order has been fully
fulfilled and billed. Operators use this to finalize an order and take it out of the
active work queue.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to close.

200.description: The updated sale order with its status set to Closed.

post.description:
Cancels a sale order, moving it from its current status (for example Open) to Cancelled.
Once cancelled the order is no longer active and no further actions such as shipping or
invoicing can be performed on it, so use this when an order won't be fulfilled.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to cancel.

200.description: The updated sale order with its status set to Cancelled.

post.description:
Reverts an Open sale order back to Quote status, useful when an order was opened prematurely
and needs further changes before it re-enters the active flow.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to revert to a quote.

200.description: The updated sale order with its status set to Quote.

post.description:
Lifts the edit lock on a sale order that was imported from a connected sale channel
(for example `Shopify`, `WooCommerce`, or `Amazon`). Channel-imported orders
are locked by default to stay in sync with the source; unlock one when you need to edit it
manually in Qoblex.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to unlock.

200.description: The updated sale order, now editable.

post.description:
Creates a new Quote sale order by copying the source order's customer, addresses, currency,
delivery date, comments, sale agent, and line items. Private notes, tags, custom fields,
attachments, payments, invoices, shipments, refunds, returns, linked orders, and status are
never copied.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to duplicate.

200.description: The newly created Quote sale order.

post.description:
Allocates available stock to the specified line items on a sale order, reserving it so the
same inventory can't be committed to another order. This is how you commit stock to an order
once it's ready to be fulfilled.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to allocate stock to.

200.description: The sale order's updated fulfillment state.

post.description:
Releases stock previously allocated to a sale order back to available inventory, freeing it
up for other orders. Use this to undo an allocation when an order is cancelled, changed, or
no longer needs the reserved stock.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to deallocate stock from.

200.description: Whether the deallocation succeeded.

post.description:
Places the specified allocations on hold, keeping the reserved stock committed to the order
but pausing it from moving forward until you explicitly deallocate or fulfill it. Useful when
an order needs to wait (for payment, a customer confirmation, or a stock check) without giving
up its reserved inventory.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order whose allocations to put on hold.

200.description: The sale order's updated fulfillment state.

delete.description:
Removes one or more custom lines from a sale order. All lines are removed together as a single
all-or-nothing operation. A custom line cannot be removed once it has been invoiced.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to remove custom lines from.

requestBody.description: The IDs of the custom lines to remove.

200.description: The full updated sale order.

get.description:
Lists the drop ship items on a sale order, the products fulfilled directly by the supplier to
the customer and bypassing your warehouse entirely. Only items flagged as drop ship on the
order are included, giving you the set you can raise supplier purchase orders for.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to list drop ship items for.

200.description: A list of drop ship items, each with its product name, SKU, quantity, and unit of measurement.

post.description:
Creates supplier purchase orders that instruct suppliers to ship goods directly to the
customer, bypassing your warehouse. Target specific line items by passing their IDs in the
request body, or omit them to process all eligible drop ship items on the order. A single
request may produce several purchase orders, typically one per supplier.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to drop ship.

200.description: The purchase orders created for the drop ship request.

get.summary: Preview Purchase Orders From Sale Orders
get.description:
Read-only preview for `POST /v1/sale_orders/create_purchase_orders` - nothing is
created. Returns every sold, purchasable product across the given sale orders, including its
already-resolved supplier if any, so a caller can assign a supplier per product (via
`supplier_assignments` on the create call) instead of every unresolved product falling
back to one blanket `default_supplier_id` or being silently skipped.

parameters.name: sale_order_ids[]
parameters.description:
The sale order(s) to aggregate line items from. Pass a single id for the details page
action, or several for the list page's bulk action - same ids you intend to pass to
`POST /v1/sale_orders/create_purchase_orders`.

200.description: Every purchasable product, its resolved supplier if any, and the products that will never be included regardless of assignment.

post.summary: Create Purchase Orders From Sale Orders
post.description:
Aggregates line items across one or more sale orders into new Draft purchase orders, one
per supplier - the backend equivalent of the "Create Purchase Order" action available both
from the sale order list (bulk, pass several ids) and a single order's details page (pass
one id). Each generated purchase order is linked back to every sale order that contributed
to it. This is unrelated to Drop Ship - the generated orders receive at the supplied
shipping location and stay Draft, awaiting normal review and approval. Use
`GET /v1/sale_orders/preview_purchase_orders` first to find out which sold products
need a supplier assigned via request's `supplier_assignments`.

200.description: The newly created purchase orders, one per supplier, plus any sold products that could not be included.

post.description:
Packs and dispatches a selection of sale orders. Set `auto_adjust` for orders held up by
wrong inventory rather than genuinely absent stock: on-hand is topped up just enough to cover
the selection and allocated to it, so orders outside the selection waiting on the same
products get none of that stock. The work runs in the background - poll the returned job for
the outcome. Orders that cannot be handled are left untouched and named in the job output;
the run is one transaction, so a failure once it starts writing rolls all of it back.

parameters.name: auto_adjust
parameters.description: Create the stock the selected orders are short of before shipping them.

200.description: The queued job. Poll it for what happened to each order.

post.description:
Uploads a CSV of sale orders and their line items and imports them in the background. The
file is checked for CSV formatting errors right away, while matching, order creation, and the
rest of the row-level validation happen asynchronously. Track progress via
`GET /v1/jobs?name=order_import` while it's queued or running; it drops off that list as
soon as processing finishes rather than settling into a final status there. When it's done,
the uploader is emailed a result summary and a matching entry appears in `GET /v1/activity`.

200.description: The queued import job to track for progress.

post.description:
Pulls orders on demand from a connected sale channel (`Shopify`, `WooCommerce`,
`Amazon`, and the like) for a date range you choose, using the same ingestion that
normally runs off channel webhooks. Use it to backfill or catch up on orders that didn't come
through automatically. Historical ranges are limited to 3 months unless your account has the
extended import range enabled. It's fire-and-forget: nothing is returned to poll, and you're
emailed a result summary once the import finishes.

200.description: The import has been queued.

post.description:
Exports the given sale orders to a CSV in the background, with one row per order item, bundle
part, landed-cost, or refund line. Up to 100 orders can be exported per request. Poll the
returned job via `GET /v1/jobs?name=sale_orders_export` until it completes; its output is
a signed, time-limited download URL for the CSV file.

200.description: The queued export job to poll for the download URL.

post.description:
Queues a background job that prints packing slips for the given Sale Orders, one per
shipment on each order, matching the legacy list page's and order detail page's "Print
packing slips" actions. Set `include_unpicked_orders` to also get a whole-order
packing slip for orders that have no shipments yet. Poll the returned job via
`GET /v1/jobs?name=print_packing_slips` until it completes; its output is a signed,
time-limited download URL for the rendered file.

200.description: The queued print job to poll for the download URL.

delete.description:
Removes one or more line items from a sale order. All items are removed together as a single
all-or-nothing operation. A line item cannot be removed once it has been shipped or invoiced.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to remove line items from.

requestBody.description: The IDs of the line items to remove.

200.description: The full updated sale order.

get.description:
Starts a background export of a single sale order's line items and custom lines
(including "Landed Cost" rows) to a CSV file. Because the export runs in the background,
this returns a job right away; poll `GET /v1/jobs?name=sale_order_line_items_export`
and read the job's output for a signed download URL once it completes.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to export.

200.description: The queued export job to poll for the download URL.

post.description:
Uploads a CSV of line items and custom lines and applies it to an existing sale order in the
background. Rows that match an existing line item's product variant (by SKU or barcode)
overwrite that item's quantity, price, discount, and tax; rows that don't match are added as
new line items. This is only available while the order is still a Quote. Poll
`GET /v1/jobs?name=sale_order_line_items_import` or `GET /v1/activity` for the result.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to import line items into.

file.description: The sale order line items CSV file.

200.description: The queued import job to poll for the result.

post.description: Attaches a supporting file to a sale order Submit the file as a multipart form upload.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the sale order.

200.description: The uploaded attachment's metadata and URL.

404.description: No sale order with this id exists in your account.

get.description:
Returns the files attached to a sale order, such as the customer purchase order, signed quote, or
delivery note, so you can keep the order's supporting paperwork in one place.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the sale order.

200.description: The sale order's attachments.

404.description: No sale order with this id exists in your account.

delete.description:
Permanently removes a previously uploaded attachment from a sale order, for example a file added
in error or no longer needed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the sale order.

parameters.name: attachment_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the attachment to delete.

200.description: Confirmation that the attachment has been deleted.

404.description: No sale order with this id, or no matching attachment, exists in your account.

get.description: Returns the payment terms configured on your account, such as Net 30 or Due on receipt. Use these to set default due dates on invoices and purchase orders and keep billing consistent across your customers and suppliers.

200.description: The list of payment terms available on the account.

post.description:
Creates a shipment for a sale order, covering either the whole order or just part of it so
you can fulfill in stages. The shipment status sets the state the shipment starts in, and
defaults to Draft when not specified.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order to create a shipment for.

200.description: The created shipment.

post.description:
Updates the details of a shipment while it is still being prepared. Changes are only allowed
before the shipment has been picked, since picking begins committing physical stock to it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order the shipment belongs to.

parameters.name: shipment_id
parameters.description: The ID of the shipment to update.

200.description: The updated shipment.

get.description:
Returns a pick plan for a shipment: a picking guide that tells warehouse staff which batches
to pull from and how much to take from each to fulfill the shipment's line items. A single
line item may draw from several batches when no one batch holds enough to cover the full
quantity.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order the shipment belongs to.

parameters.name: shipment_id
parameters.description: The ID of the shipment to get the pick plan for.

200.description: The full pick plan for the shipment, broken down by line item and then by batch.

post.description:
Marks a shipment as picked, confirming that stock has been pulled from the warehouse for
this order. Supply a pick plan to choose specific quantities and batches when you need
control over which lots go out, or send no body to accept Qoblex's recommended picks.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order the shipment belongs to.

parameters.name: shipment_id
parameters.description: The ID of the shipment to mark as picked.

200.description: The shipment, now marked as picked.

post.description:
Marks a shipment as packed, the step after picking that confirms the goods are boxed and
ready to go out. Send a request body to update the shipment's header details as part of
packing; omit it to simply advance the status.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order the shipment belongs to.

parameters.name: shipment_id
parameters.description: The ID of the shipment to mark as packed.

200.description: The shipment, now marked as packed.

post.description:
Marks a shipment as dispatched, the final step that records the goods as having left your
premises and on their way to the customer. Send a request body to update the shipment's
header details as part of dispatching; omit it to simply advance the status.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order the shipment belongs to.

parameters.name: shipment_id
parameters.description: The ID of the shipment to mark as dispatched.

200.description: The shipment, now marked as dispatched.

post.description:
Creates a delivery note for a specific shipment, capturing proof-of-delivery details such
as when it was delivered, who delivered it, who received it, and an optional signed document.
Operators use this to attach delivery confirmation to a shipment for their records.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order the shipment belongs to.

parameters.name: shipment_id
parameters.description: The ID of the shipment to attach the delivery note to.

delivered_at.description: The date and time when the shipment was delivered.

delivered_by.description: The name of the person or carrier who delivered the shipment.

received_by.description: The name of the person who received the shipment.

notes.description: Additional notes or remarks about the delivery.

200.description: The shipment with its new delivery note attached.

delete.description:
Removes line items from a draft shipment, letting you trim what goes out before the goods are
pulled. Lines on a shipment that has already been picked, packed, or dispatched cannot be
removed here.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order the shipment belongs to.

parameters.name: shipment_id
parameters.description: The ID of the shipment to remove lines from.

200.description: The updated shipment after the line items are removed.

post.description:
Assigns warehouse batches (stock lots) to the lines of a shipment, pinning down exactly which
inventory batches will fulfill each line item. Operators use this when they need to control
which lots go out, for example to ship oldest stock first or honor a customer's batch request.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order the shipment belongs to.

parameters.name: shipment_id
parameters.description: The ID of the shipment to assign batches to.

200.description: Whether the batch assignment was successfully processed.

delete.description:
Deletes a batch reservation on a shipment, releasing the reserved stock back to available
inventory. Use this to undo a batch assignment when the wrong lot was reserved or the
shipment no longer needs it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the sale order the shipment belongs to.

parameters.name: shipment_id
parameters.description: The ID of the shipment the reservation belongs to.

parameters.name: reservation_id
parameters.description: The ID of the batch reservation to delete.

200.description: The inventory transaction record reflecting the updated batch closing quantities and values.

post.description:
Records goods being sent back to the supplier against a purchase order, creating a draft supplier
return, for example to return damaged or incorrect items. The return starts as a draft; authorize it
separately once it's ready to adjust your stock.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

200.description: The new draft supplier return.

get.description:
Retrieves a single supplier return by its identifier, with its line items and any non-tracked
charge lines, so you can review what's being sent back to the supplier.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: supplier_return_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the supplier return.

200.description: The requested supplier return.

404.description: No purchase order with this id, or no matching supplier return, exists in your account.

patch.description:
Updates a draft supplier return, for example to set its number, reason, resolution, or comments
before you authorize it. Only the fields you send are changed, and updates are only allowed while
the return is still a draft.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: supplier_return_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the supplier return.

requestBody.description: The fields to change. Omitted fields keep their current value.

200.description: The updated supplier return.

400.description: The supplier return is already authorized and can no longer be edited.

404.description: No purchase order with this id, or no matching supplier return, exists in your account.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes a draft supplier return that hasn't been authorized yet, for example one raised in
error. Once a return is authorized its stock adjustment has already happened, so only drafts can be deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: supplier_return_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the supplier return.

200.description: The deleted supplier return.

post.description:
Authorizes a draft supplier return, reducing on-hand inventory to reflect the goods sent back so your
stock stays accurate. Only draft returns can be authorized.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: supplier_return_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the supplier return.

200.description: The authorized supplier return.

delete.description:
Removes a single line item from a draft supplier return, for example a product you've decided to
keep after all. Only allowed while the return is still a draft, and only when it's not the only item
left, a return must always keep at least one line.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the purchase order.

parameters.name: supplier_return_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the supplier return.

parameters.name: line_item_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the supplier return line item.

200.description: The updated supplier return.

400.description: The return is already authorized, or the line item is the only one left on the return.

404.description: No purchase order with this id, no matching supplier return, or no matching line item, exists in your account.

post.description:
Creates a new supplier so you can start raising purchase orders and bills against it right away.
Include the supplier's contact details and at least one address.

200.description: The full created supplier record, including contact details and addresses.

get.description: Returns the suppliers set up in your account so you can manage the vendors you buy from and raise purchase orders against them. Filter, sort, and page through the list to find the supplier you need.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: A filter expression used to narrow the results, for example `name@=shirt,quantity>10`. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview for the full list of operators and syntax.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: A sort expression: a comma-separated list of fields, each optionally prefixed with `-` for descending order. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview.

200.description:
A paginated list of suppliers, each with its identity, logo, and primary
            contact details. Retrieve a single supplier by id for its full contact details.

get.description:
Retrieves a single supplier's complete profile, including contact details and addresses, so you
can view or reconcile everything on file for one vendor before raising a purchase order against it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the supplier. For example, `4521`.

200.description: The full supplier record, including contact details and addresses.

post.description:
Updates an existing supplier's contact details. Any addresses included that don't match one
already on file are added; existing addresses are otherwise left as-is.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The supplier to update. For example, `4521`.

200.description: The full updated supplier record, including contact details and addresses.

delete.description:
Removes a supplier from your account so it no longer appears when raising new purchase orders.
The supplier's history on existing purchase orders, bills, and returns is preserved.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The supplier to delete. For example, `4521`.

200.description: The full profile of the supplier that was deleted.

post.description:
Creates a tax class made up of one or more components. Once created, it's available to select
on orders and products.

200.description: The created tax class.

get.description: Returns the account's tax classes, each with its components. Narrow the list by active status.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description:
Filters to apply on the tax list: property operator value.
Supported properties: `id`, `name`, `accounting_reference_id`, `tax_type`, `is_deleted`.
Supported operators: `==`, `!=`, `@=*` (contains, case-insensitive).
String values must be double-quoted. Combine multiple filters with `,` (AND) or `|` (OR).

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description:
Sorting to apply on the tax list: prefix with - for descending, no prefix for ascending.
Supported properties: `id`, `name`, `accounting_reference_id`, `tax_type`.

200.description: An array of tax classes.

get.description: Returns a single tax class, including its components.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The tax class to retrieve. Example: `42`.

200.description: The tax class.

post.description:
Updates a tax class. The name can always change. The type, rate, and components can only
change while the tax is not referenced anywhere yet - if it is, the response explains what to
fix first (for example, an existing order or a product's default tax).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The tax class to update. Example: `42`.

200.description: The updated tax class.

delete.description:
Retires a tax class so it no longer appears when creating orders and products. Blocked, with an
explanation, while the tax is still referenced anywhere - for example an account default, a
product's default tax, or an existing order, refund, return, or landed cost.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The tax class to delete. Example: `42`.

200.description: Confirmation that the tax class was deleted.

post.description:
Creates a stock transfer to move inventory from a source location to a destination
location for one or more product variants, so you can shift stock between your
warehouses. Once the transfer is created, you can assign specific batches to it before
the transfer is authorized.

200.description: The newly created transfer.

post.description:
Authorizes a draft transfer, moving the stock from the source location to the destination
location and marking the transfer as received. This is the step that actually changes your
inventory, so once a transfer is authorized it becomes read-only. For batch-tracked lines,
assign the batches being shipped via `POST /{id}/batches` before authorizing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the transfer to authorize. Example: `4821`.

200.description: The authorized transfer, now marked as received.

400.description: The transfer cannot be authorized, for example a source location has insufficient stock.

401.description: You are not authorized to make this request.

404.description: No transfer matched the given ID.

post.description:
Assigns batches to a stock transfer, recording exactly which batches are moving between
your locations and how much quantity comes from each. When you move stock that is
batch-tracked, this tells the transfer which specific batches to pull from the source
location. A single line item can draw from more than one batch.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the transfer to assign batches to. Example: `4821`.

200.description: Confirmation of whether the batch assignments were saved.

delete.description:
Removes a supplier from a variant, so you can retire sourcing arrangements you no longer use
and keep supplier records accurate. The removed supplier assignment, including its purchasing
information, is returned so you can confirm exactly what was unlinked.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product variant. Example: `4821`.

200.description:
The supplier assignment that was removed from the variant, with its supplier information and
purchasing constraints.

get.description:
Retrieves the suppliers linked to one or more variants, so you can plan procurement and
compare sourcing options in one place. The response carries supplier details, purchasing
information, minimum order requirements, lead times, and which supplier is the default.

parameters.name: product_variant_ids
parameters.description: List of product variant identifiers to retrieve supplier information for.

200.description:
The suppliers linked to the requested variants, with their purchasing and ordering
information.

get.description:
Retrieves the suppliers linked to a single variant, along with their purchasing conditions,
so you can compare sourcing options and manage buying strategy at the variant level.
Suppliers are returned in pages for variants with many sources.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product variant. Example: `4821`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: A filter expression used to narrow the results, for example `name@=shirt,quantity>10`. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview for the full list of operators and syntax.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: A sort expression: a comma-separated list of fields, each optionally prefixed with `-` for descending order. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview.

200.description:
A paginated list of the variant's suppliers with their details and purchasing constraints,
plus total and filtered counts to support paging and filtering.

put.description:
Updates the suppliers linked to a variant, letting you assign, modify, or replace supplier
relationships and their purchasing details in one request. Use it to keep procurement data
current as your sourcing arrangements change.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product variant. Example: `4821`.

200.description:
The updated list of the variant's suppliers, with their details and purchasing constraints,
plus total and filtered counts for reference.

get.description:
Returns your product variants so you can browse and sync your full catalog. Variants are
sorted by their identifier and returned in pages, letting you walk through large catalogs
without loading everything at once.

parameters.description: Products page number to return

- `images`
- `mappings`
- `locations`
- `price_lists`
- `components`

parameters.description: A sort expression: a comma-separated list of fields, each optionally prefixed with `-` for descending order. See the Filtering and sorting section in the API overview.

200.description:

get.description:
Retrieves the available values for a variant filter dimension, such as suppliers, product
types, tags, brands, locations, or the variants themselves. Use it to populate typeahead
and filter controls so users pick from real values in your account rather than guessing.
Narrow a large dimension with `search_term` or a specific set of `ids`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description:
The filter dimension to retrieve values for.
Supported values:
- `suppliers`
- `product_types`
- `tags`
- `brands`
- `locations`
- `variants`

parameters.name: search_term
parameters.description: Optional text used to narrow down the returned filter values by name.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Optional list of specific filter value identifiers to retrieve.

200.description:
Up to 50 filter values for the requested dimension, each with an identifier and a display
label, sorted alphabetically. Use `search_term` to reach values beyond the first 50.

get.description:
Retrieves the incoming stock movements for a variant, so you can see stock that is expected
to arrive but has not yet been received into inventory. Each movement links back to the
source order driving it, helping you plan replenishment and set customer expectations.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product variant. Example: `4821`.

200.description:
The variant's inventory details, including its incoming stock movements, each linked to its
source order.

get.description:
Retrieves the grouping values available for your variants, so you can organize, filter, and
analyze your catalog by the categories that matter to your business. Use it to build filters,
search interfaces, and reports over your inventory.

200.description:
The available variant grouping values for categorizing, filtering, and reporting on your
catalog.

post.description:
Links your product variants to their matching external identifiers on a third-party platform,
so orders and stock stay aligned across systems. Map many variants in one request by sending
an array of variant and external ID pairs.

200.description: A success confirmation once the external links have been created or updated.

get.description:
Retrieves your product variants alongside their external IDs, so you can see how each variant
maps to a third-party platform or integration. Filter by application or search term, or
restrict the list to only unsynced variants that have not yet been linked to an external
system, to find and fix gaps in your integration mapping.

parameters.name: app_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the external application to filter variants by.

parameters.name: search_term
parameters.description: Search term to filter variants by name, SKU, or barcode.

parameters.name: show_only_non_synced_variants
parameters.description: If `true`, returns only variants that have not yet been linked to an external system.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number for pagination.

200.description: A paginated list of variant external link records, plus a summary of the most recent record.

Fields to update on a draft manufacturing order. Only supplied header fields are changed; omit a field (send null) to leave it unchanged, or send an empty string to clear a text field. A manufacturing order can only be edited while it is in draft.

The order's component line items start as a copy of the product's bill of materials, but you can freely add, amend, or remove them per order without changing the product's bill of materials. When `line_items` is supplied it fully replaces the order's current components: include an entry with its `id` to keep/amend an existing line, include an entry without an `id` to add a new line, and omit an existing line to remove it. Omit `line_items` entirely to leave the components unchanged.

id.description: Identifier of an existing line to keep or amend. Omit to add a new line.

variant_id.description: Identifier of the product variant for this component. Required when adding a new line.

quantity.description: Quantity of this component to consume. Required when adding a new line.

wasted_quantity.description: Quantity of this component expected to be scrapped during production.

unconsumed_quantity.description: Quantity of this component expected to be reserved but not consumed.

cost.description: Unit cost to record for the component. Omit to use the variant's current moving-average cost.

UpdateManufacturingOrderLineItem.description: A component line to keep, amend, or add on a manufacturing order.

id.description: Identifier of an existing custom line to keep or amend. Omit to add a new line.

name.description: What the charge is for. Required when adding a new line.

quantity.description: Number of units of the charge (e.g. hours or runs). Defaults to 1 when adding a new line.

cost.description: Cost per unit of the charge.

UpdateManufacturingOverheadLine.description: A overhead (extra-charge) line to keep, amend, or add on a manufacturing order.

location_id.description: Unique identifier of the location where goods are received. Left unchanged when omitted.

carrier.description: Carrier used for delivery. Left unchanged when omitted.

shipping_method.description: Shipping method used. Left unchanged when omitted.

tracking_code.description: Shipment tracking code. Left unchanged when omitted.

comments.description: Notes about the receipt. Left unchanged when omitted.

line_items.description: Line item quantity updates. Line items not listed here are left unchanged.

line_item_id.description: The goods receipt note line item being updated.

quantity.description: New quantity to receive for this line item.

number.description: Custom reference number for the purchase order.

due_date.description: Expected delivery date of the purchase order.

tags.description: Tags for categorization or filtering.

comments.description: Notes visible to the supplier.

private_notes.description: Internal notes not shared with the supplier.

supplier_reference.description: Customer-facing reference number supplied by the supplier for this order.

shipping_location_id.description: The ID of the location where the order will be shipped to (Ship To). Omit to leave unchanged.

billing_location_id.description:
The ID of the billing location for the order. Must be a location that can't hold
inventory. Omit to leave unchanged.

currency.description: Currency code for the order.

currency_exchange_rate.description: Exchange rate applied to the currency at the time of the order.

is_tax_inclusive.description: Whether the line item prices already include tax.

line_items.description: Line items to add (omit Id) or update (existing Id).

custom_lines.description: Custom lines to add (omit Id) or update (existing Id).

UpdatePurchaseOrder.description:
Fields to update on an existing purchase order, including its header, line items, and custom
lines. Only supplied header fields are changed. Once the order has an authorized bill, only
Ship To (LocationId) can still change.
Line items and custom lines use the same shape as on create: entries without an
`Id` are added as new lines, entries with an existing `Id` update that line's
quantity/price (and ETA, for line items; and name/type/discount/tax class, for custom
lines). Existing lines not included in the request are left unchanged - use the dedicated
delete endpoints to remove a line.

number.description: Reference number of the supplier return. Left unchanged when omitted.

reason.description: Reason the goods are being returned to the supplier. Left unchanged when omitted.

resolution.description: How the return is expected to be resolved. Left unchanged when omitted.

comments.description: Notes about the return. Left unchanged when omitted.

line_items.description: Line item quantity updates. Line items not listed here are left unchanged.

line_item_id.description: The supplier return line item being updated.

quantity.description: New quantity to return for this line item.

number.description: The order number.

customer_reference.description: Customer-facing reference/PO number supplied by the customer for this order.

is_tax_inclusive.description: Whether the prices provided already include tax.

currency.description: The currency code for this order.

exchange_rate.description: Rate used to convert the order currency to the base currency (eg. 1 USD = 0.92 EUR.).

delivery_date.description: The date the order is expected to be delivered (ISO 8601 format).

comments.description: Public-facing notes or comments visible on the order.

tags.description: Comma-separated labels used to categorize or filter the order.

line_items.description: Line items to add (omit Id) or update (existing Id).

custom_lines.description: Custom lines to add (omit Id) or update (existing Id).

UpdateSaleOrder.description:
Fields to update on an existing sale order's header. Only supplied fields are changed.
Currency, exchange rate, tax-inclusive, and price list cannot be changed once the order has
been invoiced. Customer, origin location, currency, exchange rate, tax-inclusive, price list,
and delivery date cannot be changed once the order is closed.
Line items and custom lines use the same shape: entries without an `Id` are added as new
lines (Name/ProductVariant/Quantity/Price/TaxClassId are required for those), entries with an
existing `Id` update only the fields supplied, leaving the rest unchanged. Existing lines
not included in the request are left unchanged - use the dedicated delete endpoints to remove a
line.

id.description: Unique identifier of the custom line to update. Omit to add a new custom line.

name.description: Label describing the custom charge or adjustment. Required when adding a new custom line.

quantity.description: Quantity associated with the custom line. Required when adding a new custom line.

price.description: Unit price of the custom line. Required when adding a new custom line.

discount_rate.description: Discount rate (percentage) applied to the custom line. Defaults to 0 when adding a new custom line; omit to leave unchanged when updating.

UpdateSaleOrderCustomLine.description:
A sale order custom line to add (omit Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderCustomLineDto.Id) or update (existing Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderCustomLineDto.Id).
Adding a new custom line requires Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderCustomLineDto.Name, Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderCustomLineDto.Quantity,
Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderCustomLineDto.Price, and Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderCustomLineDto.TaxClassId; updating an existing line only changes the
fields supplied.

id.description: Unique identifier of the line item to update. Omit to add a new line item.

name.description: Display name of the product. Required when adding a new line item.

quantity.description: Number of units being ordered. Required when adding a new line item.

price.description: Unit price of the product. Required when adding a new line item.

discount_rate.description: Discount rate (percentage) applied to this line item. Defaults to 0 when adding a new line item; omit to leave unchanged when updating.

UpdateSaleOrderLineItem.description:
A sale order line item to add (omit Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderLineItemDto.Id) or update (existing Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderLineItemDto.Id).
Adding a new line requires Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderLineItemDto.Name, Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderLineItemDto.ProductVariant,
Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderLineItemDto.Quantity, Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderLineItemDto.Price, and Qoblex.Api.Sales.Dto.UpdateSaleOrderLineItemDto.TaxClassId; updating an existing
line only changes the fields supplied.

amount.description: New deposit amount, in the order's currency. Omit to leave the value unchanged.

percentage.description:
New deposit percentage of the order total, between 0 (exclusive) and 100. The resulting amount is
worked out from the order total as it stands now. Omit to leave the value unchanged.

reference.description: Your reference for the deposit. Omit to leave it unchanged.

paid_at.description: Date the deposit was paid. Omit to leave it unchanged.

UpdateSupplierDeposit.description:
Request to change a deposit that has not yet been synced to your accounting system or allocated to a
bill. Every field is optional: only the ones supplied are changed. State a new deposit value either as an
amount or as a percentage of the order total, never both, or omit both to leave the value as it stands.

name.description: New name for the tax. Can always be changed, even while the tax is in use.

tax_type.description:
New tax type. Only allowed while the tax is not used anywhere - see the error message
for what to fix first.

components.description:
New set of components (name, rate, whether it compounds on top of the others). Replaces
the existing components entirely. Only allowed while the tax is not used anywhere.

accounting_reference_id.description: New external accounting reference id. Can always be changed.

UpdateTaxClassRequest.description: Fields to update on an existing tax class.

rate.description: Tax rate percentage of this component.

is_compound.description: Whether this component compounds on top of the others.

UpdateTaxComponentRequest.description: Fields to update on an existing tax component. Only allowed while the tax is not used anywhere - see the error message for what to fix first.

reason.description: The reason or justification for creating the adjustment.

location_id.description: The ID of the location where the adjustment is applied.

number.description: Custom reference number for the adjustment. If not provided, it will be auto-generated.

comments.description: Additional notes or comments about the adjustment.

type.description:
Whether the adjustment is Simple or Advanced. The caller must specify this; it is not
defaulted server-side (defaults to Simple when the adjustment is created without it).

author_id.description:
The user the adjustment is attributed to. Defaults to the caller when omitted, and is
ignored once the adjustment is authorized. Must be a user of the caller's tenant.

product_variant_id.description: The ID of the product variant being adjusted.

quantity.description: The quantity of units to adjust.

cost.description: The unit cost of the product variant at the time of adjustment.

operation.description:
Whether `quantity` is a delta to apply (`Adjust`) or the final quantity to write
directly (`Set`). Defaults to `Set` when omitted, matching the common stocktake
"counted quantity" use case; pass `Adjust` explicitly for a +/- delta line.

UpsertAdjustmentLineItem.description: List of items included in the adjustment.

id.description: Identifier of the batch to update. Leave it out to create a new batch for the variant.

product_variant_id.description: Identifier of the product variant this batch belongs to.

location_id.description: Identifier of the location the batch is held at. Required when creating a batch.

number.description: The batch or lot number. When creating a batch and left empty, a number is generated for you.

expires_at.description: Expiry date of the batch, for shelf-life monitoring and FEFO picking.

quantity.description:
On-hand quantity for the batch. When it differs from the batch's current quantity, the change
is recorded as an auto-authorized inventory adjustment. A new batch starts at zero, so the full
quantity is adjusted in; on an update, leave it out to keep the current quantity unchanged.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Your Qoblex account is the top-level container for your business. These endpoints read and update company details, tax defaults, the currencies and manual exchange-rate overrides you trade in, your warehouse and store locations, and your subscription, billing history, and usage. Responses generally return the current account and the settings that shape how orders, stock, and pricing behave across the platform.

tags.name: Activity Feed
tags.description: The activity feed is a chronological record of notable events across your account, such as orders and stock movements your team should be aware of. Use it to surface recent activity and notifications in your own tools, and to mark entries as read.

tags.name: Adjustment
tags.description: An adjustment records a deliberate change to on-hand stock that is not a sale, purchase, or transfer, for example a stocktake correction, damage, or a manual recount. Each adjustment holds the affected variants, the counted or delta quantities, batch assignments where stock is batch-tracked, and a reconcile-then-authorize workflow. Use these endpoints to create adjustments, manage and reconcile their line items, and authorize them so the inventory ledger is updated.

tags.name: Batches
tags.description: Batches (or lots) track stock at a finer grain than the variant, each with its own batch number and expiry date, for traceability, recalls, and FEFO picking. Create and update batches, review them per variant or across the whole account, follow the batch operation audit trail, and trace a batch upstream to its origin and downstream to where it was consumed or shipped.

tags.name: Bill Payments
tags.description: Payments record money paid to a supplier against an authorized bill, reducing the amount still due. Add, correct, or remove payments as you settle each bill.

tags.name: Bills
tags.description: Bills capture what a supplier invoices you against a purchase order. Create a draft bill for the line items and landed costs received, then authorize it to record the amount owed. A bill's totals, amount paid, and amount due are the source of truth for what the supplier is owed.

tags.name: BOM & Kits
tags.description: Composition turns a simple variant into a bundle or a bill of material built from component variants. A bundle is sold and shipped as its parts; a bill of material is assembled into the finished variant through a manufacturing order, and may itself nest other bills of material for multi-level structures. Set or dismantle a variant's composition, and add, update, or remove individual components.

tags.name: Currencies
tags.description: Currency reference data: the full set of ISO 4217 codes you can assign to orders and price lists, and the current market exchange rate between any two of them. Your account's own manual rate overrides are managed under Account.

tags.name: Custom Fields
tags.description: Custom fields extend Qoblex records with your own structured data. A definition describes a field (its name, type, and where it applies) and values are attached to individual records. Use these endpoints to manage definitions and to read and assign values so your integration can carry data Qoblex does not model natively.

tags.name: Customers
tags.description: A customer is a business or person you sell to. The customer object carries identity and contact details, contacts and addresses, tax identifiers, default payment terms, and the price list that governs their pricing. Use these endpoints to list, retrieve, create, and update customers; they are then referenced by quotes and sale orders.

tags.name: Dashboard
tags.description: The dashboard endpoints return summarized, at-a-glance figures for how your business is performing, such as sales totals, costs, margins, and a period-over-period sales overview. They are read-only aggregations meant to power headline metrics and charts.

tags.name: Deposits & Refunds
tags.description: Deposits are prepayments you make to a supplier before goods ship, which you can later allocate against a bill. Refunds record money the supplier owes back to you for returned or overbilled items. Both are managed against the purchase order.

tags.name: Goods Receipt Notes
tags.description: Goods receipt notes record stock arriving against a purchase order. Create a draft as goods come in, assign batches where items are batch-tracked, then authorize the note to move the received quantities into inventory and spread any landed costs across them.

tags.name: Invoices & Payments
tags.description: Invoices record what you are charging a customer for a sale order; authorize an invoice to post the amount owed. Payments record money received against the order, reducing the balance due.

tags.name: Manufacturing Orders
tags.description: A manufacturing order describes how finished goods are assembled from their component variants. It captures the product being built, the components consumed, quantities, and batch tracking for both the inputs and the finished output. Use these endpoints to manage manufacturing orders and assign batches so production is reflected accurately in stock and cost.

tags.name: Price Lists
tags.description: A price list defines custom or tiered pricing that overrides your default sell prices for the customers assigned to it. Use these endpoints to list the price lists on your account; a customer's assigned price list then determines the prices applied on their quotes and orders.

tags.name: Product
tags.description: A product is the sellable item at the top of your catalog. Each product groups one or more variants (the individually stocked and priced SKUs) and carries shared catalog information such as name, type, and images. Use these endpoints to list products and retrieve a product with its variants; day-to-day stock, pricing, and supplier data live on the variants.

tags.name: Purchase Orders
tags.description: A purchase order is your instruction to a supplier to buy stock, and it anchors the entire inbound purchasing workflow: it tracks the supplier, ordered items and quantities, costs and landed costs, and its progress from draft through approval, receiving, billing, and payment. These endpoints manage purchase orders and their related records, including goods receipts that bring stock into inventory, supplier bills, payments, returns and refunds, deposits, attachments, and saved views. Responses return the purchase order with its items and the documents produced along the way.

tags.name: Quotes
tags.description: A quote is a priced proposal you send to a customer before it becomes a firm order. It carries the customer, proposed line items, and pricing, and can be converted into a sale order once accepted. Use these endpoints to list and manage quotes at the top of your sales workflow.

tags.name: Refunds & Returns
tags.description: Returns bring sold goods back into stock against a sale order; refunds record money owed back to the customer. Preview the amounts with the calculate endpoints, then authorize to post the result.

tags.name: Reporting
tags.description: The reporting endpoints return operational and financial reports across sales, purchasing, inventory, and demand forecasting, plus any custom reports you have saved. Each report accepts filters and returns aggregated rows and totals. Use them to pull the numbers behind your own dashboards and exports.

tags.name: Sale Orders
tags.description: A sale order is a customer's order and the hub of your outbound fulfillment and billing workflow. It records the customer, ordered line items, pricing, and the order's progress, and produces the documents that fulfill and settle it. These endpoints manage sale orders and their shipments (picking, packing, dispatch, and delivery notes), invoices, payments, refunds, returns, and stock allocations, along with saved views and CSV or sales-channel imports. Responses return the sale order together with these related records so you can reconcile fulfillment and billing in one place.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: The settings endpoints manage account-level configuration that other records depend on, such as the payment terms you offer and your locations. Use them to maintain the reusable options that appear across orders, invoices, and stock.

tags.name: Shipments
tags.description: Shipments fulfil a sale order. Create a shipment for the goods going out, pick and pack it, assign batches where items are batch-tracked, then dispatch it and produce a delivery note. Shipments are how committed stock is reduced as goods leave.

tags.name: Supplier Returns
tags.description: Supplier returns record goods sent back to a supplier against a purchase order. Create a draft return for the items leaving, then authorize it to reduce on-hand inventory accordingly.

tags.name: Suppliers
tags.description:
A supplier is a vendor you buy stock from. The supplier object holds identity and contact details,
            addresses, and the employees linked to the account, and is referenced throughout purchasing, from
            purchase orders to bills and returns. Use these endpoints to list, retrieve, create, update, and
            remove the suppliers available to your purchasing workflow.

tags.name: Tax Classes
tags.description:
Tax classes are the rates you charge or pay - a single flat rate, or several components combined
            (including compound taxes). These endpoints create, read, update, and retire tax classes,
            independently of your account's default-tax settings.

tags.name: Transfer
tags.description: A transfer moves stock from one of your locations to another, for example replenishing a store from a central warehouse. Each transfer records the source and destination, the variants and quantities moved, and batch assignments where stock is batch-tracked. Use these endpoints to create transfers and assign the specific batches being shipped.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: A user is a member of your team with access to the account. The user object carries their profile and the permissions that determine what they can see and do. Use these endpoints to list users, retrieve the signed-in user, update a user's permissions, and remove access when someone leaves.

tags.name: Variant Suppliers
tags.description: Variant suppliers are the sourcing links between a variant and the suppliers you buy it from, carrying purchasing price, minimum order quantity, lead time, and which supplier is the default. List a variant's suppliers, compare sourcing across variants, and assign, update, or remove supplier links to keep procurement data current.

tags.name: Variants
tags.description: A variant is the individually stocked, priced, and tracked item beneath a product, identified by its SKU. Use these endpoints to list and filter your variants, review their incoming stock, organize them with groupings, and map them to your external platforms. Batches, suppliers, composition (bundles and bills of material), and prices each have their own section.
